title: Machine learning predicts postoperative hydrocephalus after posterior fossa tumor surgery
summary: Seven ML algorithms were evaluated on 1073 patients from five centers (854 development, 219 external). The final model used three preoperative variables: Evans index, tumor-fourth ventricle relationship and preoperative CSF diversion status. The support vector machine reached external AUC 0.877, accuracy 81.3%, sensitivity 80.8% and specificity 81.7%, with calibration suggesting dataset shift.
ai_technology: Support vector machine among seven ML algorithms with SHAP-based feature ranking

evidence.unknown: Retrospective; dataset shift; not a stand-alone indication for CSF diversion; full text not reviewed.
